answer: Reward vesting with clawback resists sybils: earnings don't settle instantly — they vest linearly over many epochs, and the whole unvested balance is forfeited if the identity is later caught. This hands auditors a reef of time to catch fraud before value escapes. A farm can spin up a prism of fakes and farm rewards, but cannot cash out before the window exposes it; at the nadir of detection the cohort's unvested earnings are clawed back. Honest agents barely notice — their standing is durable — while disposable fakes built to grab and flee are denied the fast exit the attack needs.
